context.summary: Assessment and certification should cover the whole business IT infrastructure or a well-defined, separately managed subset.

metadata.negative_rationale: No ESAF control requires Cyber Essentials assessment or certification to cover the whole business IT infrastructure or a separately managed enterprise subset; ESAF controls are scoped to AI capabilities and assets.

context.summary: Define the network boundary.

conditions: The assessed network boundary contains in-scope AI components, flows, or enforcement points documented under ARC-110.
expected_evidence: Current AI component and data-flow diagrams showing network and enforcement boundaries.
known_gaps: ARC-110 does not define the enterprise-wide Cyber Essentials network boundary or inventory non-AI devices.
relationships.rationale: ARC-110 requires documented AI enforcement boundaries and data and control flows, directly contributing to definition of the network boundary for AI components within the assessed scope.

source_locator.locator: Section D, Cyber Essentials scope overview, page 6, opening paragraph, scope-boundary element 2

context.summary: Define the physical location.

conditions: The physical location is relevant to an in-scope AI hosting environment recorded under INF-100.
expected_evidence: Approved AI environment record identifying the hosting location and deployment inventory.
known_gaps: INF-100 is limited to AI hosting and does not require a physical-location inventory for the whole business IT infrastructure.
relationships.rationale: INF-100 requires AI workloads and supporting services to operate only in approved hosting environments, directly contributing location information for the AI-hosting portion of the assessed scope.

context.summary: Justify a partial scope to the assessor when infrastructure is excluded.

conditions: The excluded infrastructure affects the scope or determination of an ESAF assessment for in-scope AI assets.
expected_evidence: AI assessment workpapers recording scope, excluded infrastructure, rationale, and attributable supporting evidence.
known_gaps: AUD-120 is limited to AI assessment evidence; it does not establish Cyber Essentials assessor acceptance criteria or justify exclusions from general business infrastructure.
relationships.rationale: AUD-120 requires sufficient evidence for each AI assessment scope and determination, directly supporting evidence for an exclusion decision affecting the AI-system portion of a partial scope.

context.summary: Ensure all controls are implemented for in-scope cloud services, regardless of whether the applicant or provider implements them.

conditions: The cloud service supports an in-scope AI capability and provider and consumer duties are documented under ARC-140.
expected_evidence: AI cloud shared-responsibility matrix, inherited-control records, consumer configurations, and provider evidence.
known_gaps: ARC-140 covers AI-related shared responsibility and does not by itself demonstrate implementation of every Cyber Essentials control for the cloud service.
relationships.rationale: ARC-140 requires approved and monitored responsibility boundaries and validated inherited controls among AI capability owners and cloud providers, directly supporting implementation accountability for in-scope AI cloud services.

source_locator.locator: Section D(iv), Cloud services, page 9, responsibility paragraph

context.summary: Ensure a cloud provider implementing controls is contractually committed through clauses or referenced documents.

conditions: The cloud provider supplies an in-scope AI service or supporting AI control and the obligation is included in the supplier agreement.
expected_evidence: Executed cloud contract, referenced control terms, responsibility matrix, and current supplier assurance evidence.
known_gaps: CMP-120 does not prescribe Cyber Essentials-specific contract wording or cover cloud services unrelated to AI.
relationships.rationale: CMP-120 requires third-party AI obligations to be contractually assigned, verified, monitored, and enforced, directly supporting contractual commitment where a cloud provider implements AI-related controls.

context.summary: Include all organisation-owned accounts used by third parties.

conditions: The organization-owned account is used by a third party to access an in-scope AI asset.
expected_evidence: AI identity inventory showing account type, third-party user, owner, purpose, linked capability, and lifecycle status.
known_gaps: IAM-100 does not require inclusion of organization-owned third-party accounts that have no access to in-scope AI assets.
relationships.rationale: IAM-100 requires inventory and lifecycle management of every third-party identity that can access in-scope AI assets, directly contributing coverage of organization-owned third-party accounts used for AI access.

context.summary: Confirm that Cyber Essentials technical controls are met for externally managed services.

conditions: The externally managed service is an in-scope AI service or implements a control for an in-scope AI capability.
expected_evidence: Supplier assessment, assigned security obligations, responsibility matrix, assurance evidence, and remediation records.
known_gaps: CMP-120 does not itself establish every Cyber Essentials technical control is implemented or effective, including for in-scope AI services; Cyber Essentials-specific technical verification remains separate.
relationships.rationale: CMP-120 requires verification and monitoring of assigned third-party AI security obligations, contributing supplier-governance evidence relevant to assessment of an externally managed AI service.
